sort-numbers.formula:
Ascending:  sort so that a1 ≤ a2 ≤ ... ≤ an
Descending: sort so that a1 ≥ a2 ≥ ... ≥ an

The comparison is numeric (by value), not lexicographic:
2 < 10 numerically, even though "10" < "2" as text.
This is why a proper numeric sort matters — text sorting would give 10, 2.
howTo: Paste or type your numbers into the box — commas, spaces, new lines or semicolons all work.
Choose ascending (smallest first) or descending (largest first).
The sorted list appears instantly below, ready to read.
Tap Copy to put the sorted list on your clipboard.
Check the count, smallest and largest values shown underneath.
keyFacts: Numbers are compared by value, not as text — so 2 sorts before 10, unlike alphabetical sorting.
Separators can be mixed freely: commas, spaces, tabs, new lines and semicolons.
Anything that is not a number is ignored, and you are told how many entries were skipped.
Sorting is stable in effect and instant — even a few thousand numbers sort immediately.
The tool also reports the count, minimum and maximum of your list.

Input:  7, 3, 9, 1

Ascending:  1, 3, 7, 9
Descending: 9, 7, 3, 1
